blocks.text: These products raise different issues involving health, vulnerable audiences, truthful claims and social responsibility. Tobacco advertising is broadly prohibited under Australian law, with detailed restrictions and limited exceptions. Alcohol promotions must meet applicable legal requirements and relevant standards.

Fast-food marketing raises concerns about nutrition claims, portion messages and exposure of children to persuasive promotion. Do not assume the same rules apply to every product or that compliance with a voluntary code replaces legal compliance.
Identify the audience, the claim, the channel and the likely harm. Distinguish a legal restriction from an ethical concern and explain effects on trust, public image and long-term demand.

A campaign using cartoon characters to appeal to young children may generate attention but also attract criticism. A responsible alternative uses accurate information, an appropriate audience and a message consistent with relevant requirements.

The Act promotes equality of opportunity and provides remedies for unlawful discrimination, sexual harassment and victimisation in specified areas, including employment. The law is not called the Equal Opportunity Act.
In recruitment, a business should use criteria relevant to the role. A requirement that appears identical for everyone can still disadvantage a protected group without adequate justification.
Use consistent job-related selection criteria, accessible processes, respectful conduct and appropriate complaint procedures. Train staff and keep reasons for decisions.

Example: rejecting an applicant on an irrelevant assumption about a protected characteristic can create legal and reputational risk. Selecting on demonstrated skills relevant to the role supports both fairness and performance.

The Act is a major part of the national workplace-relations framework. It includes minimum standards and protections relating to workplace rights, industrial activity, discrimination and dismissal. Some WA workplaces operate under the state industrial-relations system.
The Fair Work Ombudsman provides education and compliance assistance. The Fair Work Commission is the national workplace-relations tribunal. These are different bodies.

Employees should be able to exercise applicable workplace rights without unlawful adverse action. A business needs lawful employment instruments, accurate records and a fair process when addressing performance or conduct.
Example: a manager should investigate a complaint about unpaid entitlements rather than penalising the worker for raising it. Discuss the legal obligation and the effect on trust and retention.

The Act provides a framework for protecting workers and others from work-related risks. A person conducting a business or undertaking, often the employer, must ensure health and safety so far as is reasonably practicable.
This includes safe systems of work, appropriate training and supervision, safe equipment and consultation with workers. Officers have a due-diligence duty.
Workers must take reasonable care for themselves and others, follow reasonable safety instructions and cooperate with notified safety policies.

Example: a café identifies burn risks around an espresso machine. The employer arranges maintenance, training and a safe workflow. Workers use the procedure, report defects and avoid exposing others to risk. Assigning duties to workers does not remove the employer’s responsibilities.
Labelling requirements depend on the product. Information may include ingredients, allergens, warnings, safety information and country-of-origin statements where applicable. Claims must be accurate.
A business should check the relevant regulator and current requirements before changing a label. Clear information also helps customers compare offers and use products safely.
Trading-hours rules can differ by jurisdiction, business category and location. An SME should identify the rules that apply before planning opening hours, staffing and promotion.

Longer permitted hours may create a sales opportunity but also increase wages, security and utility costs. Evaluate likely additional contribution rather than assuming longer opening always increases profit.
Children can be particularly vulnerable to persuasive techniques and may not recognise advertising. Businesses need to consider applicable law and relevant advertising standards.

Distinguish government requirements from industry codes. Analyse the product, audience, channel and message. A technically legal campaign can still harm public image if stakeholders consider it irresponsible.
